text: WFF (WF Holding, Malaysia) - analyse later; Sarantis flagged it as an unusual share that may not repeat this year. Facts so far: Oct 9 regular session opened 2.13, ran to 4.17 in the first 30 min, fell to 1.755 by 17:00-17:30 SAST, then ran to 19.44 in the 21:00-21:30 SAST bar and closed 12.29 (+499%) on about 144M shares against a float of about 38M. After hours 8.08-10.35. Oct 12 pre-market 8.91-11.86; the other list posted it at about 10.29. Oct 13 pre-market about 19.30. Prior spike Sep 25 (regular session); 1-for-5 reverse split announced Apr 9 2026. No company headline on Finviz since April; QuiverQuant called the Oct 9 move speculative trading. Not checked for IBKR tradability. Data held: full Oct 9 minute bars in the Minute data tab, and every day from Oct 12 while it stays on the watchlist (other list). To look at: what the minutes and volume did before the 17:00 low and before the second run, how volume compared with float, what happened on each following day, and which scanner filters would have caught it before the second run. Two main questions: (1) WHY did it run so high (news, filings, float and share structure, who was trading it, any promotion or social-media activity, short interest, halts)? (2) HOW could we find similar shares that could run this high (which traits it had before the move, and whether other names share them now)?
